question: How can our school cut grid electricity 30% by 2030 on an $800,000 capital budget?

plan_summary.plain_answer: You asked how the school can cut grid electricity 30% by 2030 on an $800,000 capital budget. The plan estimates that the full path (deeper efficiency work, solar on the whole usable roof and a backup battery) cuts about 31% to 46% of grid electricity, so it reaches the goal even at the cautious end. It costs about $607,530 to $1,106,329 upfront, up to $306,329 more than your budget. The version that fits the budget (standard efficiency plus rooftop solar) reaches about 28% to 42%, so it may fall just short. Rooftop solar alone covers only about 22% to 24% of your use. The building has no solar or efficiency work already, and the figure counts electricity bought from the grid. The city rates the roof not solar ready and 20 years old or more, and none of the costs include roof repair or replacement. Next: have a roofer and a licensed engineer assess the roof, then ask the Department of Citywide Administrative Services (DCAS) or the School Construction Authority (SCA) about the Solar Schools program before deciding whether to extend the budget.

plan_summary.plain_answer: You asked how to cut grid electricity 30% by 2030 and keep critical loads running in outages on $750,000. The building already has 11.4 kW of solar, and the baseline is electricity bought from the grid.
